chunk_map.heading: The summary reads better than the evidence
A customer quote no customer said
"Are you sure?" is another fluent answer

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L24 slide 2 'the opportunity tree' and L35 slide 3 'your judge' come closest: both named by the enclosing module (whats-actually-true.md include order: grow-the-tree, catch-it-making-things-up precede this lecture); spine vocabulary carve-out and module-arc carve-out apply. In-chunk pronouns ('It' L9/L11/L22) resolve to the agent/quote named in the same chunk.

Closest: slide 3 'your judge' (expanded L35) points at an earlier exercise by claim, not by position ('the opening lecture'-style phrases): grep -nE 'opening|earlier|previous' on the three slide files returns 0 body hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: expanded L35 'what would your judge show?' resolves: module whats-actually-true.md lists Exercise 'Catch it making things up' (Test four ways ... keep the winner as a judge) before this lecture. No 'the X you did/saw' phrasing in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal or demo beat; the 'Are you sure?' prompt is a described move, not a live run

rules_evaluated.evidence: Smallest chunk, slide 2 (expanded L17-24), carries a self-contained claim: an invented quote that sounds like the interviews, plus the source-per-quote move.

Closest: chunk 1 header 'The summary reads better than the evidence' (L4) vs body 'often reads better' (L7); body scopes it with 'often' and delivers stretch and smooth, so the header is true of the chunk.

Closest: slide 3 'Fluency is not evidence. Confidence is not correctness.' (expanded L33) is an anaphora pair, not a triple, no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'; slide 2 'It fits. It agrees ... reads like research' (L22) is not a verb triplet with an empty leg; no superlative self-grading ('most dangerous' L20 scoped to product work, not praise of the training); no number+retraction; no abstraction stacks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 'judge' (L35) and 'opportunity tree' (L22): ordinary module vocabulary the room earned in the preceding exercises, not repo dialect; grep for beat|mood|compendium|firing|forcing function on slide bodies returns 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n '\*\*' on the three slide files hits only maintainer-block lines (STATUS/Claims/Frameworks); 0 bold in any slide body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All three slides are structural include-links (L3, L5, L7) standing alone as paragraphs, and expand-md.js inlined all three slide files; the lecture is included by module whats-actually-true.md ('Lecture: Fluent is not true'), so it reaches the composed deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-fluent-is-not-true.md -> 'OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.'; no hand-numbered headers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-fluent-is-not-true.md -> 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Review surface, not a gate. Only links are the three structural include-links (L3, L5, L7), which the rule scopes out; no in-body links in slide text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-fluent-is-not-true.md -> 'slides: 3 ... oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 'A customer quote no customer said' (expanded L17) is a noun phrase, but it names the slide's subject and the lecture sequence's headings are otherwise claims (L4, L28); rule binds law/consolidation slides, and this one names its subject, which is the catalogue-entry carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 'Fluency is not evidence. Confidence is not correctness.' (expanded L33) restates the header's claim mid-paragraph, but it is not a closing kicker (slide ends on a question L35) and it is the slide's own explanation of the mechanism; closers on slides 1 and 2 (L13, L24) each add a move.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Covering each body: slide 3 header promises that asking 'are you sure' yields another fluent answer; L31 and L33 answer exactly that. Slides 1 and 2 bodies answer their headers; no inherited bullets from an old header (no provenance note of a retitle in the slide maintainer blocks).
